title: Thread a cable tie looped round the cords under a TV and pull it snug
instruction: Close the cable tie snugly around the three cords, then let go of it.
context: Cords under a TV or desk get bundled with a nylon cable tie. Closing one takes two hands working together: one feeds the springy 4.8 mm tip into the head's slot from the correct side, the other takes the tail as it comes through and pulls until the loop bites. Neither hand can let go early: the strap springs back out of the slot until the ratchet has caught it. Here the tie is already looped round the cords and its head held in a clip, so the task is the threading, the hand-over and the pull.
setup: Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, z up from the console top; the arm bases are at y = +0.305 (left) and y = -0.305 (right). The console is the table. A painted drywall wall stands across its far side, front face at x = 0.460, 60 cm wide and 42 cm tall. A TV hangs on the wall, stood in for by its black bottom edge (a box 4 cm deep, 60 cm wide, 8 cm tall), its bottom 34 cm above the console. A white plastic power strip (28 x 5.5 x 4 cm) lies on the console centred at (0.400, 0.000), its long side along y. Three cords run straight down from the TV's bottom edge to the top of the power strip (30 cm), gathered in a bundle: a black PVC TV power cord (7.0 mm diameter, axis at x 0.379, y -0.004), a black PVC HDMI cable (7.3 mm, at 0.379, +0.004) and a white TPE phone charger cable (3.5 mm, at 0.383, 0.000). A black nylon 6/6 cable tie (strap 200 x 4.8 x 1.2 mm with a tapered last 6 mm; head 8 x 9 x 5.6 mm with a slot through it; about 1.5 g) is loosely looped round the cords, its loop flat in the horizontal plane 17 cm above the console. Its head is held centred at (0.366, -0.010), 17 cm up, in a blue plastic clip (two jaws 10 x 6 x 1.5 mm over the head's top and bottom faces, joined by a 2 mm back plate on its robot-side face) on a vertical steel rod (5 mm diameter, 16 cm tall) standing on a 30 x 30 x 4 mm steel base on the console. The slot runs along y and opens to the left (+y). The strap leaves the head's far face (toward the wall), passes behind the cords, swings out to 7.6 cm left of the head and comes back along the robot side; its last 6 cm run straight along -y in line with the slot, the tip stopping 4 mm short of the slot's entry.
scoring: Measured on the real setup with a steel rule, a photo and a 1 s video, after the arms let go. 0 unless both grippers are at least 3 cm from the tie, the tie is still (under 1 cm/s: no part of it moved more than 1 cm over the last second), its tail has come at least 2 mm out of the head's far side and all three cords pass through the loop. Then 1.0 if at least 134.8 mm of tail has come out of the head's exit face (the loop at most 8 mm longer than the tightest it can close round the cords with the head in its clip); 0.5 if at least 117.8 mm (at most 25 mm of slack); 0.25 otherwise (threaded and closed round the cords, but loose). Success, which ends the trial, is the 1.0 condition held for 1 s. The simulation reads the same quantities from the strap's link chain: the tail is the strap's length past the slot's exit face, a cord passes through the loop when its axis lies inside the loop's outline, and clearance is measured from each gripper's TCP and pad tips.
reset_notes: A closed tie can only come off by cutting it, so each trial uses a new tie from the same bag (200 x 4.8 mm, black nylon 6/6), looped round the cords by hand to the marked start: head in the clip with the slot facing left, tip 4 mm short of the slot. The cords and the clip post do not move.
fidelity: The strap is 32 rigid 6.25 mm links on bending joints with nylon's bending stiffness, made 15 times heavier and damped for stability. The slot is 6.4 x 4.0 mm (a real one is about 5.2 x 1.6 mm with a lead-in). The ratchet is a sprung pawl that wedges, with code assisting it; the loop rests where a link joint meets the pawl, so the tail settles in 6.25 mm steps. The head is fixed where the clip holds it (clip and post have no collision); the cords are rigid. More in the README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (scripted; it reads the simulator's state)
